transcript: In Famehungry, Louise Orwin leads us through an overstimulating romp through the world of TikTok and our seemingly insatiable attention economy. In this cool cross between play, performance art, and sociological exploration, the audience basically watches Louise as she goes live on TikTok for the duration of the entire show. Now already, there's something interesting here about watching a live performance of something which is curated for an online audience. But we also get to see some projections of text which supplement and juxtapose the actions that Louise is doing for her live. This ranges from scripted and created remarks she's delivering, to real time inner thoughts, to some meta commentary on the actions themselves. It’s honestly hard to explain — but it's fascinating, satirical, and self aware. As the show progresses, it evolves into a more explicit conversation about what it means to create and consume content on a platform as enigmatic as TikTok. This piece was super interesting, and certainly one of the more innovative pieces I've seen in recent memory. And after the performance, I had the pleasure of joining Louise and some other content creators, Liz and Ashley, to talk more about the show and its themes, which feel especially relevant with the future of TikTok still unfolding. Famehungry is running at Soho Playhouse through February 9th, so catch it while you can. With that, another program for my collection.
